brief: Goldman's weekly Global Reflections argues the AI trade, having recouped most of Monday's losses and formed a double bottom, has room to grind higher as incremental AI use-case adoption creates alpha on both sides. Fed-meeting credibility anchored the long end, supporting a house view that equities trend higher into year-end, with hoped-for Consumer recovery tied to the Trump/Xi meeting and Healthcare held as an uncorrelated trade. Five points follow. Agentic AI use cases (Muse, Instinct) are eroding customer stickiness, so Goldman stays short its Consumer Inertia basket, a theme it says already hit telcos (TMUS, AT&T, VZ) on Thursday. AI power (GSX1POW1) has lagged the AI rally despite energy-inflation and regulatory headwinds, and Goldman calls positioning there washed out and near an inflection, helped by midterms and intact datacenter demand, while it stays bullish on European power (GSXERNEW). It buys US Consumer, shorts UK Consumer, long UK Homebuilders for rate relief, and long US Low Income Consumer Discretionary contingent on geopolitical relief. It prefers German fiscal-stimulus exposure over France, pairing that long with a short hedge on French Domestic ahead of next year's elections, though the pair trade has lagged recent OAT-Bund widening.
